name: aya
label: Hyperdub
lede: A Huddersfield kid who grew up under a TV mast made club music as LOFT for a decade, then sobered up and made hexed!, an album about addiction as horror film that Pitchfork rated 9.0.

eras.title: Mills, masts and a cracked Ableton
eras.text: Aya Sinclair grows up in Huddersfield under the Emley Moor transmitter, in a house full of theatre and records, and starts making music as LOFT in her teens. The town, the tower and the church that shut her out will haunt everything she records later.

years.src: DJ Mag · The FADER · The Quietus
years.h: Born in Huddersfield, raised in the shadow of a TV mast
years.p: [[aya|23f02e95-84fe-44bf-a173-f30e5c18e24d]] (Aya Sinclair) grew up in West Yorkshire near the Emley Moor transmitting station, the tower that later gives a track on her debut its name.
years.xp:
DJ Mag says both her parents worked as theatre directors and that her father introduced her to Ableton and to bands like Underworld and Leftfield. The FADER adds a household library that ran from Slipknot and My Chemical Romance to Aphex Twin and Jonathan Glazer film scores.

She told The Quietus she grew up among telecom infrastructure and textile mills. The FADER reports she taught herself on cracked Ableton and drummed in bands as a teenager.

years.h: LOFT begins: club music with the seams showing
years.p: Under the name LOFT she starts releasing experimental dance music, a run DJ Mag dates from 2009 to 2019.
years.xp: DJ Mag lists the 2016 track "Heffalump" on Astral Plane and the 2017 EP Three Settlements Four Ways on Wisdom Teeth among the notable LOFT releases. Wikipedia lists a 2016 EP, Turbulent Dynamics, and a compilation of bootlegs and edits in 2018.

eras.title: Manchester, boygirl and a name change
eras.text: She moves to Manchester, falls in with the city's experimental underground and starts a queer collective. By the end of the decade LOFT is finished and something else is starting.

years.h: Moves to Manchester, meets Iceboy Violet and Tom Boogizm
years.p: In Manchester she works with [[Iceboy Violet|7c0c5805-3e03-45ed-b049-622d287bcd4f]] and Tom Boogizm (Rat Heart), and moves in the orbit of [[Blackhaine|c1151fbd-6cbc-4c8b-b286-235a1869e56a]] and [[Space Afrika|b00bcf14-76ae-4ce9-8cae-a9077baa0849]].
years.xp: The Guardian's interview (syndicated on inkl) dates the move to 2016. The FADER lists Blackhaine, Space Afrika and Iceboy Violet as the experimental musicians she connected with while living there in her twenties.

years.h: boygirl: a queer collective built on grime and dance
years.p: With Iceboy Violet she co-founds boygirl in Manchester, a collective exploring grime, dance music and where queer people sit inside them.
years.xp: The Quietus describes boygirl as a 2017 collective that used grime and club music to explore queerness in different musical spaces. Sinclair told the Guardian she came out as trans in 2018.

years.src: The Guardian · DJ Mag · The FADER
years.h: A weekend at Pontins gives her debut its shape
years.p: The 2019 Bang Face festival, held at a holiday park, is what Sinclair points to as a key influence on her first album, Im Hole.
years.xp: She told the Guardian the Bang Face weekend at Pontins fed into Im Hole. The FADER says she changed her name around 2019, and DJ Mag dates the end of LOFT to January 2020 with the release "are eye pea ell oh eff tea".

years.h: and departt from mono games, a late LOFT EP
years.p: One of the last records under the LOFT name, released in 2019, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: aya arrives on Hyperdub
eras.text: LOFT is retired and Sinclair, now recording as aya, signs to Hyperdub. Her first album lands as a clothbound book with a record in it.

q: Something as simple as your kick pattern says so much, culturally.
years.src: Wikipedia: Im Hole · The Quietus · DJ Mag
years.h: Im Hole: poems, grime and a hymn to a transmitter
years.p: Her Hyperdub debut runs 39 minutes and comes with a clothbound book of lyrics, poems and photos co-designed with Oliver Van Der Lugt, known as Air Max '97.
years.xp:
[[Iceboy Violet|7c0c5805-3e03-45ed-b049-622d287bcd4f]] guests on "Emley Lights Us Moor". James Ginzburg mixed the record and [[Joker|4ec9883f-f359-4b41-bcf9-4d92e97f2f20]] mastered it, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork gave it 8.2 and Best New Music; it placed No. 45 on the site's 2021 year-end list and No. 2 on Crack's.

The Quietus heard grime, drill, jungle and experimental club music, with Sinclair speaking, rapping and singing in her Yorkshire accent. She told the magazine Sadie Plant's Zeros + Ones was foundational to her thinking about weaving and technology.

eras.title: Sobering up, speeding up
eras.text: Sinclair moves to London and plays constantly. In 2024 she puts out a self-released EP, and the record she is writing next comes out of the worst years behind her.

years.p: A short, self-released stopgap between the two albums, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Hexed
eras.text: The second album is an account of addiction and recovery told as horror, and it becomes one of the year's most argued-over records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hexed! · DJ Mag · The Guardian
years.h: hexed!: 34 minutes of addiction as body horror
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 9.0 and ranked it No. 22 of 2025. Metacritic scores it 91/100; The Quietus and The Wire both put it first on their year-end lists.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives the runtime as 33:59, with mixing by James Ginzburg and mastering by [[Joker|4ec9883f-f359-4b41-bcf9-4d92e97f2f20]]. DJ Mag called it "an unflinching account of addiction" built from dub metal and hypercore elements, and Paste gave it 8.5 and placed it No. 12 for the year.

Sinclair told the Guardian she chased "this sublime, other essence" through rave music until it went dark, and lost hours to dissociative panic attacks that supply the album's body-horror imagery. Score source: Wikipedia's reception section for Hexed! (Pitchfork's own page was not fetched).

years.h: The FADER's GEN F: nine months and two weeks sober
years.p: In the profile, 31-year-old Sinclair says she made hexed! as a way of inducing her own therapeutic trance, and now tours most of the year from Peckham.
years.xp: The FADER also reports she was pushed out of a Pentecostal church at 16 when peers learned she was queer, which set off years of substance use and dissociation.
